previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of recurrent arterial and venous thromboses, asplenia, COPD, and chronic pain presented with chest pain and was found to have a new aortic arch thrombus on CT imaging despite being on chronic enoxaparin therapy. He was admitted for evaluation and management, with vascular surgery deeming the clot too high-risk for intervention. Hematology recommended transitioning from a heparin drip to therapeutic enoxaparin, initiating aspirin, and increasing simvastatin to 40 mg daily. A repeat anti-Xa level confirmed therapeutic anticoagulation. The patient's pain was managed with oral oxycodone, and he was discharged home with close follow-up planned for hematology, repeat imaging in one month, and ultrasound evaluation of an incidental renal lesion. His chronic pain and prior narcotic contract violations were noted, with recommendations for long-term pain management.

___ year old man with a history of chronic thrombosis of unclear

violations of narcotics contracts, who presents with pleuritic

# Chest pain, Atypical: Pleuritic in description, and in the 
setting of known hypercoagulability. Initially concerning for 
DVT/PE. However, both LENIs and CTA negative. CK Normal. Concern 
for ACS ruled out with TnT and repeated EKGs that were at his 
baseline.  Patient is on Lovenox ___ID and notes he is 
compliant.  Other potential source of pain could be ventral 
Spigelian hernia that may have worsened or simply irritated 
nerve endings in that area.  Could be MSK or persistent pain 
from micro thrombi. Ultimately the etiology of this pain is 
unclear, but it is not a worrisome source at this time.  Patient 
was able to ambulate on his own without exacerbation in pain, no 
relief with rest, no diaphoresis.  Patient was continued on 
Oxycodone 15 mg QID as per PCP. 
- TRANSITIONAL
--- PCP follow up for pain control and Reflux control
--- Hematology f/u with Dr. ___ in heme/onc regarding 
hypercoagulability on ___ at 3:20 ___
--- Continue home Lovenox ___ BID
--- Continue home aspirin 325 mg
--- Cont home simvastatin 
--- Pain control OxycoDONE (Immediate Release) 15 mg PO/NG 
Q6H:PRN pain
.
# Right leg pain: Pain described as sudden and intense, located 
in the right groin and started on day of arrival.  Initial 
concern from patient was in regards to his IVC Filter, CTA here 
ruled out any obstruction or clots around the IVC Filter.  No 
evidence of DVT on lower extremity duplexes.  Patient had good 
arterial pulses throughout his extremities.  Ultrasound was 
negative for hematoma.  Improved over time on its own.  Patient 
did not have neurovascular compromise: FROM, no swelling, 
symmetrical strength. No pallor/paresthesia, pulses intact. 
Patient endorses feeling muscle tightness, so pain may represent 
muscle spasm. Electrolytes were WNL. Minimal concern for 
arterial thrombi given above physical exam. Patient was able to 
ambulate on his own without difficulty and on day of discharge 
did not have mobility issues. 
- TRANSITIONAL
--- Monitor as an outpatient
.
